title: Roku Delivers Another Stellar Quarter: Q3 Sales Soar 24% as Media and Entertainment Ad Spending Sees Biggest Growth in Four Years
description:
Roku‘s financial engines are cranking in overdrive ahead of the streaming platform company’s takeover by Fox Corp. next year.

	For the third quart
body:
Roku‘s financial engines are cranking in overdrive ahead of the streaming platform company’s takeover by Fox Corp. next year.

	For the third quarter, Roku handily topped Wall Street earnings expectations, with top-line growth of 24% to $1.50 billion in revenue. Total gross profit was $649 million, up 24%, and Roku generated net income of $183 million — up more than seven-fold from the year-prior quarter.


	In Q3, Roku’s Platform segment revenue grew 23% year over year to $1.3 billion, with both advertising and subscriptions sales growing 23%.
	

	According to Roku, similar to Q2, political advertising on its platform in Q3 exceeded the comparable quarter from the 2024 U.S. presidential election cycle. Advertising in the company’s media and entertainment category also outperformed: Roku said the most recent quarter was the highest year-over-year revenue growth for M&E in four years “as media companies invested on the Roku platform to promote their content and services.”

	Total streaming hours consumed across Roku in Q3 were 39.9 billion, up 9% year over year. Revenue in Roku’s Devices jumped 33%, $194 million. The company operates the Devices business as a loss-leader with a negative margin; in Q3, the operating loss for the segment was $48.6 million (a -25% gross margin), driven primarily by higher memory costs.

	Fox Corp. on June 15 announced a deal to buy Roku for $22 billion, which is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2027. As with its second-quarter earnings, Roku is not hosting an earnings call or providing financial guidance, citing the pending Fox acquisition.
	

	The pending acquisition by Fox “is an extraordinary opportunity to accelerate our vision, allowing us to scale faster and innovate more aggressively for viewers, partners and advertisers,” Roku’s founder and CEO Anthony Wood, and Dan Jedda, CFO and COO, said in a letter to shareholders.

	The execs said in the letter: “We are building a diversified and durable business by focusing on monetization initiatives: deepening integrations with third-party advertising platforms, growing Roku-billed subscriptions, and enhancing the Roku Experience. With our open platform, we help our content partners attract and retain audiences, and we offer advertisers the ability to reach viewers at scale, all while providing viewers with an outstanding streaming experience.”

	Following the close of the Fox acquisition, Wood will have an ongoing role at the combined company and will join the Fox board.

	Pictured top: Disney+ “Toy Story 5” home screen takeover on Roku

schema.headline: Roku Delivers Another Stellar Quarter: Q3 Sales Soar 24% as Media and Entertainment Ad Spending Sees Biggest Growth in Four Years

title: Jessica Alba Battled ‘Major Impostor Syndrome’ as She Built The Honest Company Into an Early Star-Led Business Success Story
description: Jessica Alba was nine months pregnant, stressed out of her mind and battling a bad allergic reaction to laundry detergent when she decided to launc
body:
Jessica Alba was nine months pregnant, stressed out of her mind and battling a bad allergic reaction to laundry detergent when she decided to launch her first business.

	Alba spoke about her experience as a successful entrepreneur in a conversation with Courtney Kelso, senior executive VP and head of payments: consumer and small business for U.S. Bank and Visa, held Oct. 29 in Hollywood. Alba, the actor known for such films as “The Fantastic Four” and “Sin City” and James Cameron’s Fox TV drama “Dark Angel,” was recently named spokesperson for U.S. Bank on behalf of small businesses. She’s featured in a national ad campaign rolling out for U.S. Bank’s Business Essentials Visa Card.
	

	Alba’s determination to launch a company that used safe and healthy chemicals in skin care and cleaning products was realized after the birth of her daughter. The Honest Company made its retail debut in 2012 with a handful of products. Nine years later, the company had a successful IPO, making Alba one of the youngest and one of the few Latinas to take a company public.

	In the conversation with Kelso, moderated by Cynthia Littleton, Variety’s co-Editor in Chief, Alba recalled the hard work of getting the company off the ground. She was ahead of the curve in recognizing that her name recognition could be harnessed to create awareness for her brand.

	“I didn’t slap my name on a brand that already existed. I didn’t collab with the brand that existed. I did something impossible. I created something that never existed, and to build a consumer brand around a digital marketplace, which also had not been done before,” Alba said. “I was really trying to solve something, I had to learn about operations, supply chain. I had to learn about shipping and packing. [Alba and her initial partners] were literally getting different types of bubble wrap around our detergents and throwing them off the back of the cars because we’re like, that’s going to happen when said delivery person is irritated in the middle of winter in Ohio, they will be tossing it and so we had to see if like the cap would break. And it did, it totally did.”
	



	

					Jessica Alba and U.S. Bank’s Courtney Kelso at the U.S. Bank and Visa Present An Evening With Jessica Alba, in Partnership With Variety on October 29, 2026 in Hollywood. (Photo by Katie Flores/Variety)
									Variety via Getty Images
	



	The learning curve was steep, Alba admitted to the invitation-only crowd of small business owners, entrepreneurs and business influencers.

	“We launched with a beta website because entrepreneurs don’t know that you shouldn’t launch with the beta website,” she said. And then there was the time that they had to chase after consumers for payment because the system failed to charge credit cards. “You sent them the product, and then you have to call them because you are also customer service and you say, ‘Excuse me, can I please charge your credit cards because you have the products and we didn’t really charge it last month.’ ”

	Kelso confidently assured Alba that her experience was not unusual.

	“Small business owners have these wonderful characteristics of entrepreneurialism and resiliency, and it’s no surprise that 30 million small businesses in this in this country with more than 60 million jobs are responsible for half the country’s GDP,” Kelso said. “It’s about ingenuity, it’s about what you see and how you can solve [a problem], and the determination to get it done. That is what makes small businesses the force that they are in the American economy.”

	Kelso added that the rising Gen Z generation is predisposed to think about launching business, in part because of the role models provided by Alba and other determined stars-turned-entrepreneurs.

	“Millennials and Gen Z entrepreneurs are driven by purpose. They more optimistic than other generations that are starting businesses,” Kelso said. “They start them as passion projects. They start them on the side in some cases. We find that they are creating them at a faster clip and faster rate, and they are more optimistic and deeply connected to what they are building.” Keslo complimented Alba for being “the role model for the scaling of that kind of business.”

	Determined as she was, Alba also had to fight off her own insecurities about her ability to succeed in the business realm. She came from modest means, with both of her parents serving in the military.
	

	“I had a major impostor syndrome about whether I was even worthy of running a business because I had been an actress since I was 12. I graduated with a GED at 15, and I’m surrounded by venture capitalists and all these people in business that know so much more than me,” Alba said. “I can imagine that entrepreneurs, especially if it’s your side hustle before it becomes the main hustle, you’re like, ‘Can I really do this?’ But you have to be scrappy about it.”

schema.headline: Jessica Alba Battled ‘Major Impostor Syndrome’ as She Built The Honest Company Into an Early Star-Led Business Success Story

title: Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses
description:
Meta is helping bring Lionsgate‘s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” to 3D screens — and its upcoming VR glasses.

	The studio and tech com
body:
Meta is helping bring Lionsgate‘s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” to 3D screens — and its upcoming VR glasses.

	The studio and tech company have partnered to convert the film to 3D ahead of its Nov. 20 release, marking Meta’s first time working with a studio on such a conversion. The process was done in collaboration with DNEG, which has helped convert films including “Dune: Part One,” “Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire” and “Venom” from 2D to 3D.
	

	The 3D version will also be available on Meta’s new $1,299 VR glasses when they release in the spring. Jim Packer, Lionsgate’s chief revenue officer, called the collaboration a “compelling example of how technology can transform existing formats to create fresh, new experiences” in a statement.

	“As we continue to explore new ways for audiences to experience ‘The Hunger Games,’ we’re thrilled to partner with Meta on this first-of-its-kind collaboration,” Packer said. “[Director] Francis Lawrence has created an incredible 3D experience for ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,’ and we’re excited for audiences to experience it in theaters and then on Meta VR Glasses.”

	Lawrence said the 3D adaptation gave the team another way to let audiences experience the journey of Joseph Zada’s Haymitch Abernathy, a younger version of the character originated by Woody Harrelson, whom audiences follow through the 50th edition of the Hunger Games.

	“From the beginning, we wanted ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to feel visceral and immersive, pulling audiences deep into Haymitch’s experience,” said Lawrence. “I’m excited for people to see the film on the big screen and ultimately experience it in an entirely new way on Meta’s VR glasses.”
	

	Meta unveiled the VR glasses at its Meta Connect event in September, promising immersive versions of “Avengers: Infinity War” and “Star Wars: A New Hope” plus 3D versions of “The Avengers,” “Black Panther” and select Lionsgate titles. Sarah Malkin, Meta’s head of entertainment at its Reality Labs, said the new “Hunger Games” represented “the kind of cinematic experience that will be phenomenal in theaters, and also showcases what this technology makes possible at home.” 

	“We’re delighted to work with Lionsgate and Francis Lawrence to bring the film in 3D to audiences around the world,” she added in a statement.

schema.headline: Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses

title: ‘X-Men’: ‘Hunger Games’ Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel’s Reboot
description: After battling it out in the arena in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” and leading the latest “Karate Kid” installment, Ben Wang is circl
body:
After battling it out in the arena in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” and leading the latest “Karate Kid” installment, Ben Wang is circling another major franchise: Marvel Studios’ “X-Men” reboot.

	Wang is in negotiations to play Bobby Drake, aka Iceman, who was one of the founding X-Men. Created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, the character first appeared in “The X-Men #1” in September 1963.


	 If the deal closes, Wang would join a sprawling cast that features Sadie Sink (as Jean Grey), Kit Connor (as Cyclops), Samara Weaving (as Emma Frost), Inde Navarrette (as Rogue), Maya Boyd (as Storm), Asa Germann (as Angel), Christopher Abbott (as Professor Charles Xavier) and Adam Driver (as Mr. Sinister).
	

	Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige revealed the new “X-Men” cast at the D23 convention in August, after Sink’s Jean Grey debuted in the blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” The upcoming movie reboots the mutant team for the first time since the 2019 Fox film “X-Men: Dark Phoenix” and for their first outing under the Marvel Studios umbrella. Jake Schreier, who oversaw last year’s “Thunderbolts,” is directing the film from a script by Lee Sung Jin and Joanna Calo. “X-Men” is set for release on May 5, 2028.

	In “Sunrise on the Reaping,” Wang plays Wyatt Callow, one of the tributes from District 12 alongside Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), who is the focus of the “Hunger Games” prequel movie. Wang has also starred in Lionsgate’s “The Long Walk,” Francis Lawrence’s adaptation of the Stephen King classic, as well as Will Ropp’s coming-of-age comedy “Brian,” David Wain’s comedy “Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass,” the 2024 “Mean Girls” reboot, and the Disney+ projects “American Born Chinese” and “Chang Can Dunk.” He is repped by Stewart Talent, Artists First and Schreck Rose Dapello.
	

	Deadline first reported Wang’s potential involvement in the project. Marvel Studios could not be immediately reached for comment.

schema.headline: ‘X-Men’: ‘Hunger Games’ Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel’s Reboot

title: How to Watch CNN’s 2026 Midterm Election Coverage Live Online: Streaming Options, Anchors and Key Races to Follow
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	CNN is ge
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	CNN is gearing up for extensive coverage of the 2026 midterm elections on Tuesday, Nov. 3 with Jake Tapper and Anderson Cooper leading the network’s primetime special.

	The network’s “Election Night in America” special begins at 4 p.m. ET with Tapper and Cooper co-anchoring live from Washington D.C. Dana Bash will focus on key Senate races, while Kaitlan Collins will report on reaction from  President Donald Trump and his administration. Meanwhile, John King will return to CNN’s interactive Magic Wall to break down results as ballots are counted across the country.
	

	The best way to stream CNN’s election coverage live online is through a live TV streamer such as DirecTV, Sling TV and Hulu + Live TV. 

	DirecTV includes the network in its live-TV packages and its more affordable MyNews genre pack. The latter currently costs $39.99 per month for the first two months, increasing to $44.99 afterward, and comes with a five-day free trial for eligible new subscribers. The package also includes Fox News, MS NOW and other news channels.

	DirecTV is also bringing back its Election HQ feature from Nov. 2 through Nov. 4, allowing viewers with compatible equipment to watch CNN, Fox News, MS NOW and Newsmax simultaneously, alongside live election results provided by the Associated Press. 

	CNN is also available on both Sling Orange and Sling Blue, including Sling a special News and Election Multiview feature that lets subscribers follow four news networks at once. Sling Blue’s lineup includes CNN, Fox News, MS NOW and ABC News Live, while Sling Orange includes CNN, LiveNOW from Fox, ABC News Live and CBS News 24/7.
	

	For viewers looking for free election coverage, Sling Freestream will carry programming from outlets including CBS News 24/7, ABC News Live and NBC News NOW, although the full CNN cable feed requires a paid subscription.

	CNN’s election coverage will begin earlier in the day, starting at midnight ET with Elex Michaelson, followed by Erica Hill at 3 a.m., Audie Cornish at 5 a.m. and John Berman, Kate Bolduan and Sara Sidner at 7 a.m. Cooper will take over at 10 a.m., followed by Wolf Blitzer and Erin Burnett at noon.

	Throughout the evening, Burnett will anchor a panel from Texas, one of this year’s most closely watched Senate battlegrounds. Other contributors include David Chalian, Kasie Hunt, Pamela Brown, Laura Coates and Tom Foreman, with political commentary from David Axelrod, Scott Jennings and Van Jones. Berman and Bolduan will take over overnight coverage at 2 a.m. Wednesday.

	The stakes are particularly high for this year’s elections, the first nationwide vote since Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate races are on the ballot, with Republicans defending their narrow congressional majorities. Democrats are hoping to regain control of at least one chamber, which would significantly alter the legislative landscape for the remainder of Trump’s presidency.

	Among the Senate races drawing national attention are contests in Maine, where Republican incumbent Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson; Texas, where Democrat James Talarico is challenging Republican Ken Paxton; and Ohio, where former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown is attempting a comeback against Republican incumbent Jon Husted. Competitive contests in Michigan, Iowa, Alaska and Kansas could also help determine the Senate majority.

	CNN will have more than 25 correspondents reporting from key states, including Texas, Maine, Michigan, Georgia and Alaska, as well as coverage from the White House.

	Viewers can also watch directly through CNN’s newly expanded All Access streaming subscription, available through CNN’s website, app and supported connected-TV devices.

schema.headline: How to Watch CNN’s 2026 Midterm Election Coverage Live Online: Streaming Options, Anchors and Key Races to Follow

title: ‘Sex Education’ Star Asa Butterfield Signs With Linden Entertainment (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Linden Entertainment has signed actor Asa Butterfield for representation.

	Butterfield most recently made his stage debut in Barney Norris’ “Secon
body:
Linden Entertainment has signed actor Asa Butterfield for representation.

	Butterfield most recently made his stage debut in Barney Norris’ “Second Best” at Riverside Studios in London, which was based on David Foenkinos’ best-selling novel of the same name, and starred in Oscar Boyson’s “Our Hero, Balthazar.”

	Known for his role as Otis Milburn in the Netflix comedy “Sex Education,” Butterfield will next be seen as the Beatles’ manager Brian Epstein in BBC’s “Hamburg Days,” which follows the band’s formative years in the German city, as well as John Carroll’s comedy “Happy” alongside Kyra Sedgwick, Mark Strong and Wyatt Russell.
	

	Butterfield made his screen debut when he was just 8 years old in ITV’s “After Thomas” and went on to star in Mark Herman’s “The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas” just two years later, which earned him a nomination for Most Promising Newcomer at the British Independent Film Awards. 

	His additional credits include Martin Scorsese’s “Hugo,” James Graham’s “A Brilliant Young Mind,” Peter Chelsom’s “The Space Between Us” opposite Gary Oldman, Tim Burton’s “Miss Peregrine’s Home for Peculiar Children,” Gavin Hood’s “Ender’s Game” and Susanna White’s “Nanny McPhee and the Big Bang” opposite Maggie Smith, Ralph Fiennes and Ewan McGregor.

	Linden was founded in 2020 by Nicole King and Stacy O’Neil, who lead the company alongside JoAnne Colonna and Riva Marker. Their client roster includes talent such as Vin Diesel, Jennifer Garner, Eva Longoria, Amy Adams, Eiza González, Brendan Fraser, Forest Whitaker and Connor Storrie.

title: Driven Unveils Original Programming Slate, Including Series Starring Tom Nelson, Emelia Hartford and Tanner Foust (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Automotive enthusiast-centric interactive streaming platform Driven has unveiled its initial original programming slate beginning with “Art of Spee
body:
Automotive enthusiast-centric interactive streaming platform Driven has unveiled its initial original programming slate beginning with “Art of Speed” starring renowned engine builder Tom Nelson.

	First announced last December, Driven comes from car-enthusiast co-founders including longtime producer Michael George, “Top Gear USA” host Tanner Foust and “Gran Turismo” actor Emelia Hartford.


	Additional original series include programs starring automotive talent like Hartford (“Gran Turismo”), Foust (“Top Gear USA”), Ben Collins (“Top Gear”), Ant Anstead (“Wheeler Dealers”), Jenson Button (Formula 1 World Champion), Tom Nelson (renowned car builder), Antron Brown (award-winning drag racer) and more. 
	

	Per Driven, this starting lineup will “anchor a library of content from established and emerging creators, and complement conversations in dedicated communities where enthusiasts can connect, discuss their interests, share projects, and exchange knowledge.”

	Driven unveiled its original series lineup ahead of its upfront presentation to advertisers, which is scheduled for Nov. 3 at SEMA in Las Vegas. According to the company, the platform’s initial beta program has brought in more than 15,000 users over the last few months and “helped shape the platform’s technology, features and community experience, with members continuing to influence its development.”

	The ad-supported, subscription-free platform is available on iOS, Android, web, Apple TV, Google TV, and Amazon Fire TV, with additional connected-TV platforms planned.

	“We built Driven to bring premium storytelling and authentic car culture together,” Driven CEO Michael George said. “Enthusiasts want to go deeper into the people, the craft and what’s really at stake. These four originals deliver that – without fabricated timelines, fake ticking clocks, or manufactured drama. The ambition, setbacks, and breakthroughs are real. Driven is giving those stories a home, and look forward to sharing them with our audience.”
	

	Additional series premiering exclusively on Driven in early 2027 will include “Pikes Peak” (starring Tanner Foust, Jenson Button and Ant Anstead), “Queen of the Mountain” (starring Emelia Hartford) and “Go or Go Home” (starring NHRA champion Antron Brown).

	Descriptions for each series, provided by Driven, can be found below.

	ART OF SPEED

	Six 1-hour episodes. Starring Tom Nelson. Created and Directed by Michael George. Produced by Emelia Hartford. Executive Produced by Michael George, Matt Swanson and Tom Lofthouse.

	The man behind the most powerful street cars on earth, and the over five years it took to build them.

	Tom Nelson left street racing to build a company around what he understood better than anyone: horsepower. Nelson Racing Engines became the place you go when 1,000 horsepower is the starting point, and the cars that roll out of his Chatsworth shop have gone on to Hollywood, to magazine covers and to the kind of owners who want something nobody else has. Art of Speed was shot over five years inside that shop. Each episode follows one build from a bare block to the first time its owner turns the key, including Maximus, the twin-turbo Charger built for Furious 7, and F-Bomb, David Freiburger’s 1,500-horsepower Camaro. The engines are the easy part. The hard part is everything around them: the deadlines, the customers, the physics, and a builder who has never once accepted the number on the dyno as the final answer. It ends in Iceland, with a machine on roads it was never meant for.

	PIKES PEAK

	Three 1-hour episodes. Starring Tanner Foust, Ant Anstead and Jenson Button. Directed by Tom Lofthouse and Dan Hack. Produced by Jake Cardew and Ed Sanders. Executive Produced by Michael George and Tom Lofthouse.

	One hundred days to build a car. One mountain to prove it.

	A customer handed Radford Motors a million dollars and told them to build whatever they wanted. Ant Anstead decided to race it up America’s deadliest road before delivering it. One hundred days on the clock, a company that had never raced anything, and a car nobody had driven in anger. Ant and Jenson Button put Radford’s name on it. Joe Scarbo and Martin Jung built it. Tanner Foust, who has raced almost everything with wheels, agreed to take it up 12.42 miles of mountain with no barriers where it matters, in a car that was still being finished the week it shipped. No insurance if it crashes. No second attempt if it fails. Pikes Peak: A Race to the Clouds follows the whole thing, from a bare chassis in a California shop to practice mornings above the treeline, through the breakages, the all-nighters and the clashes, to a result nobody saw coming: Radford’s first race ever, and a win.
	

	QUEEN OF THE MOUNTAIN

	One 90-minute documentary. Starring DRIVEN co-founder Emelia Hartford. Featuring Jeff Zwart, Tanner Foust, Betim Berisha, and Robin Shute. Executive Produced by Michael George and Tom Lofthouse.

	12.42 miles. 156 corners. One run. The mountain decides.

	A year ago Pikes Peak sent DRIVEN co-founder Emelia Hartford home before the summit. So she built a car to go back: a brand new Corvette ZR1, 1,064 horsepower to the rear wheels, a cage she welded herself, and a crew she moved to Colorado for a month. Race week nearly broke the program. Her carbon wheels were banned mid-week, the car failed tech, and two days out she was tearing it apart to re-weld the cage while the coolant boiled over. Then the green flag. Ten minutes and eleven seconds later, she was the fastest woman ever up Pikes Peak, in the fastest rear-wheel-drive production car the mountain has seen, on her first run to the top in the race’s 104th year. Queen of the Mountain tells the story behind that time, featuring Jeff Zwart, the champion who coached her corner by corner, Tanner Foust, Betim Berisha, and Robin Shute, the veterans who know what fast really costs up there, and the question none of them can quite answer: why this road, at this price, every June. Emelia’s answer is already in. Just wait till next year.

	GO OR GO HOME

	Three 30-minute episodes. Starring Antron Brown. Directed by Ben Carter. Produced by Lisa Hughes Kennedy. Executive Produced by Michael George and Tom Lofthouse.

	A season inside NHRA drag racing, where runs last under four seconds and every driver says goodbye to their family before strapping in.

	Top Fuel dragsters are the fastest accelerating machines on earth. Go or Go Home spends a season with the people who drive them and the people who pay for them: four-time champion Steve Torrence, who nearly died twice before he ever sat in a race car. Antron Brown, racing toward the win most drivers want, at Indy. And the young drivers and family-run teams trying to stay on the track against billionaire budgets. Shot across Bristol, Sonoma, Charlotte and the U.S. Nationals at Indianapolis, with full access to the pits and the homes behind them. The results are in there. What stays with you is the rest of it: fathers and sons, the money it takes, the fear nobody talks about, and the hour between rounds when a crew tears an engine down to nothing and rebuilds it.

title: Sanfic Mórbido Lab Lineup Ranges From an LGBTQ Alien Monster Comedy to a Mapuche Parable, Extreme Horror and Cold War Sci-Fi
description: Simón and Raimundo Bucher’s “L4IK4,” Roberto’s San Sebastián’s “The Hostess” and Javier Attridge’s “Beneath the Flesh” weigh in as potential stando
body:
Simón and Raimundo Bucher’s “L4IK4,” Roberto’s San Sebastián’s “The Hostess” and Javier Attridge’s “Beneath the Flesh” weigh in as potential standouts at the 7th edition of the Sanfic Mórbido Lab, now a fixture on Latin America’s genre scene, part of Sanfic Industria, which runs Nov. 2-8 in Santiago de Chile.

	In its totality, however, with five titles from Latin America and one from Spain, the 2026 Sanfic Mórbido Lab underscores the vitality and variety of the region’s genre, ranging from Cold War sci-fi (“L4IK4”) to extreme horror (“The Hostess”), Mapuche identity parable (“Beneath the Flesh), gay alien monster masculinity comedy (“Chupacu”), realist adult horror (“Spring Curse”) and a mix of folk horror and social observance (“Tonalli”).
	

	If one common denominator runs through at least four of the titles, however, is their grounding in Latin American reality as its genre assumes the arthouse mantle of movies as a reflection of social malaise, whether blow-hard machismo, identity shame, AI or miracle faith culture.

	“L4IK4” marks the first feature from Simón Bucher, a rising star of Chilean animation, creator of the eye-catching animated sequence in Chilean box office smash “Denominación de Origen”

	“The Hostess” is the first feature for 10 years of San Sebastián and writer Guillermo Guerrero after the cult – and divisive – “The Night of the Virgin” (2016), hailed by Bloody Disgusting as “disgustingly unforgettable” and selected for the Fantasia and Mórbido .

	In another return, “Beneath the Flesh” is written and directed Javier Attridge whose multi-prized Prime Video pick-up “Wekufe: the Origin of Evil” was praised by Ain’t It Cool News as a “smart and tension filled little found footager.”
	

	Repping a second debut at Sanfic Mórbido Lab, “Chupacu” is inspired by the creepypasta legend of a gay alien monster

	“Chupacu,” which literally means “ass-sucker.” It is written and directed by Brazilian-Argentine Antonia Baudouin and produced by Rodrigo Carneiro, a partner at Carneiro Verde Filmes and producer of Gustavo Vinagre’s “Three Tidy Tigers Tied a Tie Tighter” a Berlinale 2022 best feature Teddy Award winner.

	Underscoring the potential quality of this year’s lineup, another Lab title, “Spring Curse,” reps the latest from Pablo Vergara, behind “Ojos verdes rojos malditos,” a Buenos Aires Rojo Sangre best director and screenplay winner in its Argentina competition.

	The lineup also includes “Tonalli,” the latest from Jesus “Chiva” Rodríguez, whose 2015 drug-run nightmare “The Bosses” broke out as a cult item among fans, placing No. 8 among that year’s Top 10 movies at Mexico box office.

	A close look at the titles:

	“Beneath the Flesh,” (“Lo que duerme bajo la carne,” Javier Attridge, Panóptico Films, Chile)

	Attridge’s follow-up to 2017’s “Wekufe,” returning to Chile’s south with a young Mapuche woman who hides her heritage behind an online sexual persona. In her homeland, something begins to grow beneath her skin each time she sacrifices a part of herself to belong. “I’m troubled by how shame can be passed down through generations,” Attridge tells Variety, calling the project “visceral psychosexual horror, where the violence of the past resurfaces beneath the skin.”

	“Chupacu,” (Antonia Baudouin, Carneiro VerdeFilmes, Brazil)

	The latest from Brazilian queer cinema powerhouse Carneiro Verde. At a testosterone-fueled barbecue held at a gaudy mansion in Brazil’s agribusiness heartland, a terrifying alien monster Chupacu assaults its ultra-macho revellers… one ass at a time – forcing the men to rethink masculine pleasure. A “very stylized gore horror-comedy about the straight man’s fear of anal pleasure,“ says Baudouin, writer of horror comedy “Furnas Fundas,” which opened last month in Brazilian cinemas.

	“The Hostess,” (“La Anfitriona,” Roberto San Sebastián, Monndo,CSC Films, Plátanobolígrafo, Spain)

	“‘The Hostess’ is a cruel, sophisticated and deeply disturbing exploration of our darkest human instinct: the need to inflict pain in order to feel alive. On others and on ourselves. A visceral and unforgettable cinematic experience that will leave no one untouched,” San Sebastián promises. Lead produced by Bizkaia-based genre/emerging talent producer Monndo with other Basque outfits CSC Films and Plátanobolígrafo.
	

	“L4IK4,” (Simón Bucher, Raimundo Bucher, La Mazmorra Studio, Chile)

	In an alternate Cold War universe, a dachshund is sent as an experiment to the first virtual world. Facing Earth’s doom, a scientist dives into the network to save her and transcend physical death through mutual love and loyalty. Described as a 3D, stop-motion and pixilation hybrid, produced by Santiago-based La Mazmorra Studio. Simón Bucher also co-directed a Vimeo Staff Pick, the grand guignol “The Feast,” a Universidad Católica graduation short selected for 2025’s Annecy Animation Festival.

	“Spring Curse,” (“Maldición en primavera,” Pablo Vergara, Coruya Cine, Argentina)

	From Vergara, also writer-director of the series “Cuentos para viernes por la noche. A young Uber driver and her uncle give a ride to a mysterious doll, after which they are pursued by an AI digital presence. “Realist adult horror, working classic genre elements, pictured with an aesthetic contaminated by daily life where I live,” says Vergara, based out of Argentina’s Córdoba.

	“Tonalli,” (Jesus “Chiva” Rodriguez, Tirando Terror, Mexico)

	The latest from Chiva, known for “The Bosses” and road movie “Metaflm.” A young trans punk in the hard-scrabble Mexico City neighborhood of Tepito appeals to Santa Muerte for her life to change. It does, but those around her begin to die. “Via folk horror and Tepito urban realism, the film tackles marginal existence, identity and the need to believe from a profoundly Mexican perspective,” Chiva tells Variety.



	

									Courtesy of Jesus ‘Chiva’ Rodriguez

title: Screen Savers: Magic Walls, Big Boards Become Critical to TV-News Election Night Success
description: John King was phoning from Maine, but his most important calls won’t take place until Tuesday night.When King takes up his regular position at CNN’
body:
John King was phoning from Maine, but his most important calls won’t take place until Tuesday night.When King takes up his regular position at CNN’s “Magic Wall” during Election Night coverage, he will do so with a new layer of digital bell s and whistles at his command. He has a floating “Key Race Leaderboard” that shows how the closest races are tracking in real time. And he will be able to show viewers whether costs of gas, rent and groceries have gone up or down in every county and precinct, so viewers can see whether rising costs appear to play a role in how voters from each party cast ballots.


	“It’s a powerful visual,” says King, who has manned CNN’s signature voting-data board since 2008, when a former CNN Washingotn bureau chief, David Bohrman,discovered the technology on display at a military-intelligence trade show. The system was originally designed to help Pentagon analysts utilize a touch-sensitive screen to map out their work in real time.
	

	Such technology isn’t just there to dazzle the eye. For the nation’s big TV-news networks, the feature has become increasingly critical to business as well.

	Viewers have long been accustomed to seeing King and others such as Fox News’ Bill Hemmer and NBC News’ Steve Kornacki manipulate colorful screens on set and rattle off stats and data. Indeed, the element has become so de rigueur that none of the networks can envision an Election Night telecast without it. The anchors might spotlight a specific viewer’s home county or state, and the visuals make the process of distilling numbers, percentages and exit polls much easier. At MS NOW, Ali Velshi works the board. Ed O’Keefe keeps up on stats for CBS News and Rachel Scott and Rick Klein oversee the task for ABC News. CNN also has Harry Enten and Phill Mattingly on tap.

	Now, these correspondents stand increasingly at the center of new products and content presentations the networks hope keep viewers focused on their screens, and not someone else’s. NBC News is counting on Kornacki not only to charm TV viewers with his data insights, but to entice digital followers with a stand-alone “Kornacki-cam.” So important is Kornacki’s presence to both program, that NBC is tapping new technology that will let the correspondent stay in the NBC News TV studio even as he talks directly to the digital crowd by blocking his voice from the linear audio feed.
	

	“We never want Steve to have to stop talking, and we prefer not to put Steve in a different space,” says Marc Greenstein, an NBC News executive vice president who oversees many aspects of Election Night coverage . It’s crucial, he says for NBC News anchors like Savannah Guthrie and Tom Llamas “to instantly interact” with Kornacki during the night.

	Meanwhile, MS NOW will stream a YouTube feed giving its viewers a look at Velshi, and is running a contest to win one of his signature vests. “You won’t hear the audio, but you will get the point,” says Velshi, who notes that followers will gain an understanding “of what the team determined what is going to be important to cover and why.”

	Fox News Channel’s Bill Hemmer and his “Bill-board” have been a years-long mainstay of Election Night coverage. This year, says the anchor, his data will be used to create a “brilliant graphic we can cast out on to the studio floor” that lets viewers “watch the vote count come in to the counties that matter. Our audience will be able to see where the votes are coming from and why or why not we have called a particular state.”

	ABC News will introduce a new feature called “Vote Shift” that examines how voters in each country may have changed their attitudes since 2024. “When President Trump won, we saw a really dramatic shift across all states toward the Republicans, even in the states that voted for Kamala Harris,” says Jenn Metz, executive producer, special events and news specials planning at ABC News. “This time, we are able to visualize how voters are shifting in real time.”

	In an era when the networks are competing more directly with independent journalists and so-called “creators” who lead newsletters, YouTube streams or video podcasts, the data boards, walls and screens given them a gee-whiz edge over their indie rivals. The information is seen as “reliable. It’s accurate. You can trust it,” says King. And only a news organization with money and resources can put such a system in place. All that can reassure viewers who wonder where the nation is headed. “Elections make people tense. You’re on a side. You want to see if your party, your team wins. Our elections of late are so close,” King notes, and displaying the underpinnings of how people vote and why may offer some reassurance.

	Critics worry that the digital screens create a sense of “gamification” around one of the country’s most serious nights, particularly at a time when more viewers have grown interested in online wagering and prediction markets. Combined with orchestral theme music and other flourishes, the boards may add to a sense of drama rather than toning it down.
	

	Hemmer believes the influx of local data can be reassuring, with even people in the studio “drawn to the locations they are more familiar with.” He may be directed to focus on certain areas of the country where a tight race is unfurling, but he will also look for interesting local stories. If he thinks there’s something of significance in a certain area, “I will find a way to get there as well.”

	Still, there is something to be said for not deluging the viewer in on-screen gimmicks and graphic flashes. The technology, after all, was initially created to offer viewers a simple distillation of voting trends. “You don’t’ want to overdo it,” warns King., “There are people out there who question election integrity, who say people are trying to rig the elections, who say you can’t trust the media,” he says. “We want to make it better when we can. We also want to be careful not to complicate it so people say ‘What did they do?’”

	Mastering the screens and the data behind them takes weeks of study as well as work with hand motion. “It is brute force learning, on a daily basis,” says MS NOW’s Velshi. Hemmer is known to study at the New York Public Library to ensure he has a quiet space for learning the granular details of voting patterns and political conditions around the country. King practices on a “miniature version” of the Magic Wall on an iPad. “If I have free time can move around and make suggestions about how to make it more user friendly, he says.

	An update to the software or the features creates a situation not unlike an upgrade to an iPhone, says Hemmer. “You have to learn a new trick, and that’s exciting every couple of years.”

	Another important skill? Knowing how to get out of a glitch on live TV.

	Elections tend to bring a wider swath of viewers than typically watch the news networks. And while digital boards are fun to look at and can hook new audiences, an unexpected pause for buffering displays can be agonizing as the counts keep coming in. “How do you get out of a situation where you don’t want to be, and how do you do it clean and quick, so the audience doesn’t get confused with what they are watching?” asks Hemmer. “That takes practice.”

	Drilling down into very granular areas poses another kind of test. Local color can be great, says King, unless the details are wrong. If you travel “to somebody’s home and talk about the politics there and the texture of the community, you’ve got to get it right.”
	

	Chances are the news outlets will continue to find more uses for the boards, not fewer. It’s easy to envision future election and primary “multi-casts” in which different people examine the boards for different kinds of data, with each getting their own live stream. The screens transform reams of data into easy-to-understand images, illustrations and diagrams, and when it comes to TV, says Velshi, “the visual sense is stronger than the auditory sense.”

title: Invercine, Gema Films and Gaman Cine, Top Producers on Latin America’s Film-TV Scene, Bring to Market New Productions
description: Invercine, Gema Films and Gaman Cine, top producers on Latin America’s film-TV scene, will bring to market their latest productions at Sanfic Indus
body:
Invercine, Gema Films and Gaman Cine, top producers on Latin America’s film-TV scene, will bring to market their latest productions at Sanfic Industria in its industry centerpiece, WIP Iberoamericana.

	Turning on Alejandro Zambra, one of Latin America’s most-read novelists whose “Poeta Chileno” is currently being adapted by Oscar winning Sebastián Lelio (“A Fantastic Woman”), “Zambra,” directed by Paula Leonvendagar, is backed by Invercine.
	

	Led by Macarena and Matías Cardone, the Chilean production house has proved a pioneer on Latin America’s premium series scene, behind top-notch premium series such as “News of a Kidnapping,” “Dignity,” “Ramona” and “Mary & Mike.”

	Directed by Agustina Pérez Rial, “The Other Voice,” an intimate first-person portrait of Mercedes Sosa, is lead produced by Nicolás Gil Lavedra (“Las grietas de Jara”) at Argentina’s Gaman Cine, co-founded with Emiliano Torres, director of “El invierno.”

	The debut of DP-turned-helmer Marchesini Weihmuller, nominated for his cinematography on Clarisa Navas’ “One in a Thousand,” “Hot Springs” is produced by Gema Juárez’s Allen’s Gema Films, behind “Reas,” ”The Castle” and “Pornomelancholy.”

	Co-producing WIP Iberoamericana title “The Grass Along the Path,” Cinestación, headed by Dominga Sotomayor (“La Perra”) and Omar Zúniga (The Strong Ones”), was also behind “Chile ’76.”

	“The Grass Along the Path” is directed by Fernando Lavanderos, one of the mid-2000s “Novíssimo” Chilean Cinema movement which heralded the emergence of a clutch of young star auteurs. Nicolas Videla, a leading director on Chile’s LGBTQ scene, helms “The Criminal Record of Madame Wittmann.”
	

	Leonvendagar, Pérez Rial and Marchesini Weihmuller are just beginning their careers, as are other directors of titles at WIP Iberoamericana.

	The industry strand, for example, will highlight a second chance later life dramedy from Panama’s Mariel García Spooner whose debut, 2021’s “Algo Azul,” proved a HBO Max U.S. pickup and Prime Video buy for Latin America, and “Las Visitantes” from Afro-Colombian producer-director Yurieth Romero Velásquez, producer of the Premios Macondo nominated short “El hombre sin cabeza.”

	“The Cry of Serankwa,” marks the second feature from Yull Núñez, whose debut, “El Silencio de los Palafitos,” scored an honorable mention at Miami’s Ibero-American Film Festival, and is spoken in Iku, an Indigenous language in Colombia’s highest mountains.

	A closer look at the eight titles:

	“The Cry of Serankwa,” (“El grito de Serankwa,” Yull Núñez, Cinequipos Producciones, Colombia)

	In Colombia’s mountains, two Iku people best friends Marcelo and Anibal prepare a rite to save the world from ecological decimation. The ritual fails and Anibal departs the mountains for a big city. Years later, now a mining engineer, he returns with a project that threatens his ancestral village’s ecosystem and his friendship with Marcelo, the new guardian of the mountains. The film “invites us to reflect on our relation with the environment, life and death,” Nuñez tells Variety.

	“The Grass Along the Path,” (“Las hierba de los caminos,” La Forma Cine/Cinestación)

	Pinky, an insecure teenager, is part of a socially diverse gang marked by violence and rigid gender roles, which are challenged when he meets Valentina. A Chilean coastal town coming of age drama recreating the social milieu of 1990. The latest from Lavanderos, also director of fest favorite “Lost North” and Chilean smash hit documentary “Eterno.” “Grass” is produced by Clara Taricco (“La Once,” “Yo no soy de aquí,” “Los Niños”).

	“Hot Springs,” (“Las termas,” Armin Marchesini Weihmuller, Argentina)

	Over 80, Evangelina and brother Luis vacation briefly at a hot springs hotel spa. He talks 12 to a dozen, which riles Evangelina, but they love and depend on each other. A touching hybrid vision of old age, its infirmities and resilient zest for life. “A film built around apparently trivial conversation, but every word and silence talks about the passage of time, of bodies which fail and an obstinacy to go on living,” Marchesini Weihmuller tells Variety.
	

	“The Other Voice,” (Agustina Pérez Rial, Gaman Cine, Fiørd Estudio, Mercado Films, Lorolo, Vorágine, Unafilms, Argentina, Spain, Brazil)

	The great Argentine folk-singer Mercedes Sosa came across on stage as an imposing warm stage presence and an unyielding champion of the poor. “The Other Voice” delivers a more intimate first-person portrait of Sosa, exiled from Argentina over 1979-82: desperately lonely, fragile and homesick. “When I sing, nobody notices my pain,” she writes to friend Hugo Otero in one of the over 100 letters on which the film in based. A revelatory doc-feature.



	

					Mercedes Sosa in ‘The Other Voice’
	



	“The Criminal Record of Madame Wittmann,”(“El Prontuario de Madame Wittmann,” Nicolas Videla, Anastasia Benavente, Cinespecie, Chile)

	The return to Chile of legendary transsexual vedette Evelyn Wittmann, now 73, whose life story crosses with lost documentary “Prontuario,” from Hernán Garrido. The latest from Videla (“Naomi Campbel,” “El Diablo es Magnífico,” “Travesti Odyssey”), Benavente and Cinespecie, respectively protagonist and producer of “Travesti Odyssey.”

	“La Residencia,” (Mariel García Spooner, Hello October, Panama)

	Three friends in their mid-60s, facing financial uncertainty and fearing loss of independence, unite to create a seniors’ social club. Starring Colombia’s Xilena Aycardi and Marcela Carvajal, a triple Málaga Festival WIP winner, gathering industrial support as it moves through its final stages of post-production ahead of festival launch. “The film explores friendship, the fear of growing older and above all the possibility of starting over without losing who you are,” says García Spooner.



	

					‘La Residencia’
	



	“Las Visitantes,” (Yurieth Romero Velásquez, La Caracola Films, Belle Films, Pablo Mondragón, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Mexico)

	Five women cross paths every Sunday in the entry line of a prison, united by the incarceration of their loved ones, making them face the same pivotal decisions, such as seeking freedom or confronting the past. Their lives intertwine even more after the escape of two prisoners, planned by two of the women. “Born from a personal experience, ‘Las Visitantes’ focuses on women, especially Afro-Caribbean, who sustain, care and resist from outside, revealing the emotional loads, shame and emotional economies implied by loving someone in prison,” says Romero Velásquez.
	


	“Zambra,” (Paula Leonvendagar, Invercine, Tierra de Juego Foundation, Chile)

	The engaging “Zambra” follows poet Alejandro Zambra in Mexico on his daily round with his young son, buying chiltepe, battling with his latest novel, expanding it to rewrite, his possible inspiration in his grandmother, and back in Chile, at a book signing and reflecting on literature an an escape from chronological time. “A profound reflection on literature, exploring the nature of its language, the creative processes through which it emerges and the technology it represents,” Leonvendagar (“Creo“) tells Variety.



	

					‘Zambra’

San Antonio Spurs Love Triangle
                          Woman Linked To Tony Parker Cheating Scandal Dies by Suicide
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 2, 2026
                            11:49 AM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 2, 2026
                                1:08 PM PST
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A woman once linked to Tony Parker during his marriage to Eva Longoria has died by suicide ... years after the alleged affair rocked the San Antonio Spurs.
      
    
            Erin Benavides, who was previously married to former Spurs player Brent Barry, was found dead at 54 inside a home in Port Aransas, Texas, on October 14 ... after police responded to a welfare check prompted by an alarming text message she reportedly sent to a friend of her husband.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to the San Antonio Express-News, officers forced their way into the home and discovered Erin with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities do not suspect foul play, though the investigation remains active.
      

            Erin made headlines back in 2010 when she was accused of having an affair with Tony, who was married to "Desperate Housewives" star Eva at the time ... while Erin was married to Tony's former Spurs teammate Brent.
      
    
            The drama exploded after Eva reportedly discovered hundreds of text messages between Tony and another woman, later identified in reports as Erin ... sparking rumors of an affair that Erin publicly denied. Tony also reportedly denied any physical relationship.
      
    
            Both marriages ultimately fell apart ... Eva filed for divorce from Tony in November 2010, while Brent and Erin also split around the same time.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Erin later became an attorney, working as an assistant district attorney in Texas and handling human-smuggling cases. She also advocated for children in foster care and victims of trafficking.
      
    
            Her former boss, District Attorney Christina Mitchell, remembered her for her dedication to her work, sense of humor, and love for her sons.
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

            The passengers on the private jet that crashed in Florida have been identified ... they were a family of four from Texas ... and they were traveling with their nanny and two friends ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Onboard the Learjet 60 that crashed Sunday were 44-year-old Austin tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, plus his wife Helen, their two kids, and two close friends ... sources close to the family tell TMZ.
      
    
            The Robinsons had their nanny with them ... and the two pilots also died.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We broke the story ... the captain was 55-year-old Jeff Gregory.
      
    
            His co-pilot was 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha. She earned her pilot's license when she was just 17 years old, doing so before she even graduated high school.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The private jet was flying from Austin to the Bahamas when it took a nosedive and crashed in Florida. Video shows the jet plummeting from the sky, nose-first, as it explodes on a busy street.
      
    
            The NTSB held a news conference Monday, confirming ice began forming on the jet in the middle of moderate turbulence. The crew asked to increase altitude from 35,000 feet to 37,000 feet shortly before an emergency was declared.
      
    
            RIP

            Lil Durk has been placed in solitary confinement at the Metropolitan Detention Center in L.A. ... TMZ has learned.

            Here's the deal ... sources with direct knowledge tell us ... Durk's cell has been "constantly searched," but prison authorities haven't found any contraband since he was acquitted in the murder-for-hire case.

            Meanwhile, the Bureau of Prisons is staying mum on the situation.
      
    
            A BOP spokesperson tells TMZ ... "For privacy, safety, and security reasons we do not discuss the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, including housing assignments, potential disciplinary infractions, or internal security measures."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As you know, Durk was found not guilty in his murder-for-hire trial back in September. He still faces felony charges for racketeering and firearms.
